newsitem.title: HONG KONG: April unit says Merrill quits role in sale.
newsitem.headline: April unit says Merrill quits role in sale.

text.p: Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings Ltd unit Riaupulp said Friday that U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch has resigned as an opinion provider for one of Riaupulp's asset sales.
"Merrill Lynch has resigned and been replaced," W. Michael Verge, Riaupulp finance director, told Reuters from Jakarta. He declined to say which bank had replaced Merrill.

In December, Merrill had provided a "fairness opinion" on Riaupulp's sale of a power plant to Riau Prima Energy, but Verge said that the investment bank had recently resigned from its position as opinion provider.
Verge said that because of Merrill's resignation, the closing of the power transaction, which had been scheduled for mid-January, will be delayed.
"We plan to proceed as stated with the power transaction and anticipate no problem," said Verge.

Rumours of the investment bank's resignation had swirled around bond markets. Riaupulp's sale of the power assets and a planned sale of chemical assets obliges a mandatory redemption of US$300 million in outstanding Yankee bonds of Riaupulp's RAPP International Finance.
The obligation also affects US$250 million in outstanding secured bank debt.
But Verge said that the delay in the US$266 million power sale closing will not change any of the terms of the redemption clause.
The clause requires Riaupulp to retire all its outstanding secured debt at 101 percent of the principal amount if collateral sales exceed 25 percent of the company's book value.
Officials at Merrill Lynch were not available for comment on the resignation.
SBC Warburg is the opinion provider for Riaupulp's proposed sale of US$140 million in chemical assets to Inti Indorayon Utama, another member of the April group.
Verge denied rumours that SBC also had quit.
The sale of chemical assets, which requires the approval of Indorayon shareholders, is expected to go forward in late February.
